pr_title: Make stats summary tests more flexible
pr_body:

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Summary API test is a bit [flaky on ubuntu right now](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet/1313556070618107904), and it also [fails on CRIO/Fedora CoreOS](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/95343) because the output of `/stats/summary` isn't same.

I'm waiting for a [kubernetes](https://github.com/orgs/kubernetes/people) member to verify that this patch is reasonable to test. If it is, they should reply with `/ok-to-test` on its own line. Until that is done, I will not automatically test new commits in this PR, but the usual testing commands by org members will still work. Once the patch is verified, the new status will be reflected by the `ok-to-test` label.

I understand the commands that are listed [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=kubernetes%2Fkubernetes).

<details>

Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md).  If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [kubernetes/test-infra](https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/issues/new?title=Prow%20issue:) repository.
</details>

Flaky test issue - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/95344
Test grid link of flaky tests - https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-release-master-blocking#node-kubelet-master
Sample failed test - https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-node-kubelet/1313556070618107904
Failure on CRIO/Fedora CoreOS - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/95343

Apart from fixing the [flake](https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-release-master-blocking#node-kubelet-master), this PR also fixes the assumptions on the platform that may not be true on CRIO/Fedora Cores. Here is the sample output of `/stats/summary` from CRIO/Fedora CoreOS, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/95343#issuecomment-704748920
Keeping this PR only focused on `UsageNanoCores`,  I have purged the other changes in this PR and will handle them in separate PR if needed.

Additional question that came to mind @harche 

> Summary API test is a bit flaky on ubuntu right now, and it also fails on CRIO/Fedora CoreOS because the output of /stats/summary isn't same.

Did you manually run this test on fedora or is there a testgrid dashboard where this test is being executed in fedora?
If you ran manually, how many times did you run it? how many failures did you see? what was your setup?

@alejandrox1 I use following command to run node e2e on Fedora CoreOS,

```
make test-e2e-node REMOTE=true RUNTIME=remote IMAGE_CONFIG_FILE="/home/harshal/Downloads/image-config-cgrpv1.yaml" INSTANCE_PREFIX="harpatil" CLEANUP=false CONTAINER_RUNTIME_ENDPOINT="unix:///var/run/crio/crio.sock" FOCUS="\[HEYHOTEST\]" SKIP="\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]|\[Serial\]" TEST_ARGS='--kubelet-flags="--cgroup-driver=systemd --cgroups-per-qos=true --cgroup-root=/ --runtime-cgroups=/system.slice/crio.service --non-masquerade-cidr=0.0.0.0/0" --extra-log="{\"name\": \"crio.log\", \"journalctl\": [\"-u\", \"crio\"]}"
```

the image config file is from, https://github.com/harche/crio-fcos-config/blob/master/image-config-cgrpv1.yaml

But it needs some more patches (PRs still not merged) to successfully launch the node e2e job on Fedora CoreOS host. 

I have run those jobs several times, but the failures due to 0 value of `UsageNanoCores` very actually very rare with FCOS host. To be precise, out of hundreds of host I have seen it just twice. So that issue is not as frequent on FCOS as on Ubuntu.

Interesting, wondering how to follow up to actually run these tests in fedore.
One last thing to merge, @harche could you please add some comments on the test itself summarizing the reason why, please?
ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95345#discussion_r504057582

I think this change may be a good thing to experiment but it will also be helpful to have some comments to go along with the code to iterate on this test - otherwise the values seem somewhat arbitrary.

@alejandrox1 I added a comment with a link that provides the information from this discussion over here. 

About running the Fedora CoreOS based tests, I have WIP PR, https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/pull/19342 that will add some pre-submit prow jobs. I am also working on adding some periodic jobs as well. Once those are merged in test-infra, we should be able to trigger the jobs and observe the results on testgrid for Fedora CoreOS based nodes.

[APPROVALNOTIFIER] This PR is **APPROVED** This pull-request has been approved by: *alejandrox1*, *harche* The full list of commands accepted by this bot can be found [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=kubernetes%2Fkubernetes). The pull request process is described [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/owners.md#the-code-review-process)
Needs approval from an approver in each of these files: - ~~[test/e2e_node/OWNERS](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/OWNERS)~~ [alejandrox1] Approvers can indicate their approval by writing `/approve` in a comment Approvers can cancel approval by writing `/approve cancel` in a comment
Shouldn't we only get a 0 value on the very first scrape?  This sounds like a bug, rather than something we should relax tests for.

issue_context.title: Summary API test is a bit flaky
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about flaky tests or jobs (pass or fail with no underlying change in code) in Kubernetes CI -->

**Which jobs are flaking**:
[Kubelet-node-master](https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-release-master-blocking#node-kubelet-master)

**Which test(s) are flaking**:
[Summary API NodeConformance](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/summary_test.go#L41)

**Testgrid link**:
https://k8s-testgrid.appspot.com/sig-release-master-blocking#node-kubelet-master

**Reason for failure**:
Based on the execution conditions sometimes the value of `Node.SystemContainers[pods].CPU.UsageNanoCores` could be 0 instead of expected 10000

**Anything else we need to know**:
- links to go.k8s.io/triage appreciated
- links to specific failures in spyglass appreciated
